about: Bylonder's implementation registry: each Blender unit an export uses, by Blender's identifier, and the implementations a page can run it with, each with its license and fidelity. A key ending in * stands for every identifier with that prefix; a more specific key comes first. Status planned: not built yet.

transform.implementation: page runtime (blend-scene.js) composing location, rotation and scale

action.implementation: Babylon AnimationGroup, Hermite keys where they are the F-curve

clean-room F-Curve unit (runtime/fcurve-evaluator.js, drivers/fcurve.js): an object transform's F-Curve Babylon cannot play exactly (rotations, easings, extrapolation, Cycles), its keys in scene.bin; modifiers but Cycles stay baked
sampled per frame from Main (Bake Animation, or what the unit does not reproduce)

driver:SINGLE_PROP.implementation: clean-room driver units (runtime/drivers/, docs/clean-room/), run by the page's scheduler once a control the driver reads is set

driver:TRANSFORMS.implementation: clean-room driver units (runtime/drivers/, docs/clean-room/), run by the page's scheduler once a control the driver reads is set; rotation readings differ from Blender in about 0.3% of random cases, at float32 branch boundaries

driver:LOC_DIFF.implementation: clean-room driver units (runtime/drivers/, docs/clean-room/), run by the page's scheduler once a control the driver reads is set

driver:ROTATION_DIFF.implementation: clean-room driver units (runtime/drivers/, docs/clean-room/), run by the page's scheduler once a control the driver reads is set; rotation readings differ from Blender in about 0.3% of random cases, at float32 branch boundaries

driver:SCRIPTED.implementation: clean-room expression unit (runtime/drivers/expression.js); an expression needing Python stays baked

fcurve:driver.implementation: clean-room F-Curve unit (runtime/drivers/fcurve.js), a driver's own F-Curve; Continuous Acceleration smoothing and modifiers but Cycles stay baked

armature.implementation: Babylon Skeleton, the pose sampled from Main

modifier:NODES.implementation: Blender's module (the Blender fallback, bylonder-blender/, with Include Source .blend), its float, integer and boolean inputs set by path

ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled.implementation: Babylon PBRMaterial (a material of one Principled BSDF)

CompositorNodeGlare.implementation: Blender's GLSL made at export on the blocks library's pass block (bylonder-blocks.js); Fog Glow, which reads its highlights back on the CPU, passes its image through

CompositorNode*.implementation: Blender's GLSL made at export (a pixel node's code with its values as uniforms, or an operation's recorded plan of passes) on the blocks library's pass block (bylonder-blocks.js, MIT OR Apache-2.0); a value that changes the code or the plan needs Blender's evaluator

world:probe_clamp.implementation: Babylon's math blocks in the exported world material: the color scaled until its largest component is at most the Sun Threshold, then the indirect clamp, as Blender's manual describes them (https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/eevee/world_settings.html, Sun Threshold; https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/eevee/render_settings/light_paths.html, Clamping); the brightness measure, the largest component, observed in Blender 5.2.3's EEVEE (a world of (8, 2, 1) at Sun Threshold 4 lights a white sphere (3.93, 0.98, 0.49), at indirect clamp 3 (2.93, 0.73, 0.36): the ratio kept, the largest component at the limit)

view_transform.implementation: view transform extension (bylonder-view-transform.js): Standard as sRGB's encoding, other views and looks through a lattice of Blender's display processor computed at export (data; the license of Blender's color management files is still to be checked)
